sec: Compensatory limits in acute and chronic respiratory disorders · p829

items.q: Match the compensatory limits table — 1) Respiratory acidosis, acute  2) Respiratory acidosis, chronic  3) Respiratory alkalosis, acute  4) Respiratory alkalosis, chronic … A) ↓up to 12–14 mEq/L HCO₃⁻  B) ↑up to 30 mEq/L HCO₃⁻  C) ↓up to 20 mEq/L HCO₃⁻  D) ↑up to 45 mEq/L HCO₃⁻
items.exp: Compensatory limits: respiratory acidosis acute ↑up to 30 and chronic ↑up to 45 mEq/L HCO₃⁻; respiratory alkalosis acute ↓up to 20 and chronic ↓up to 12–14 mEq/L HCO₃⁻. (Book p829)

items.q: In chronic respiratory acidosis, HCO₃⁻ compensates up to:
items.exp: Chronic respiratory acidosis: ↑up to 45 mEq/L HCO₃⁻ (acute: ↑up to 30 mEq/L). (Book p829)

items.q: In acute respiratory acidosis, the HCO₃⁻ ceiling is:
items.exp: Acute respiratory acidosis: ↑up to 30 mEq/L HCO₃⁻. (Book p829)

items.q: In acute respiratory alkalosis, HCO₃⁻ compensates down to a floor of:
items.exp: Acute respiratory alkalosis: ↓up to 20 mEq/L HCO₃⁻; the chronic state falls further. (Book p829)

items.q: The lowest printed HCO₃⁻ value in the compensatory limits table is:
items.exp: Chronic respiratory alkalosis: ↓up to 12–14 mEq/L HCO₃⁻ — the lowest value in the table. (Book p829)

items.q: A patient with chronic respiratory alkalosis has an HCO₃⁻ of 11 mEq/L. How do you read this against the table?
opts: It is below the printed chronic floor of 12–14 mEq/L, suggesting an additional metabolic acidosis
It is exactly at the acute limit of 20 mEq/L
It is within the chronic limit, so the picture is fully explained
It exceeds the chronic ceiling of 45 mEq/L
items.exp: Chronic respiratory alkalosis compensates only down to 12–14 mEq/L; a value of 11 mEq/L lies beyond that printed limit. (Book p829)

items.q: ‘Chronic respiratory acidosis allows a higher bicarbonate ceiling (45 mEq/L) than acute respiratory acidosis (30 mEq/L).’
opts: True — the printed ceilings are 30 mEq/L acute and 45 mEq/L chronic
False — the acute ceiling is higher than the chronic ceiling
False — both states share a ceiling of 20 mEq/L
True, but the chronic ceiling is 12–14 mEq/L
items.exp: Table: respiratory acidosis ↑up to 30 mEq/L (acute) and ↑up to 45 mEq/L (chronic). (Book p829)

items.q: All but one of these row values of the compensatory limits table are correctly quoted. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Chronic respiratory alkalosis — ↓up to 20 mEq/L HCO₃⁻
Acute respiratory acidosis — ↑up to 30 mEq/L HCO₃⁻
Chronic respiratory acidosis — ↑up to 45 mEq/L HCO₃⁻
Acute respiratory alkalosis — ↓up to 20 mEq/L HCO₃⁻
items.exp: The chronic respiratory alkalosis limit is ↓up to 12–14 mEq/L; the 20 mEq/L figure belongs to the acute row. (Book p829)
